standard_prerequisites.name: Cartesian and cocartesian squares in an abelian category
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the epimorphism and monomorphism facts about the canonical projections and coprojections that give uniqueness of the connecting map and the commutativity of its defining diagram.

standard_prerequisites.name: Kernels from cartesian squares
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the epimorphism from x onto the kernel of the projection pi used in the construction of the connecting map.

standard_prerequisites.name: Testing exactness through a fibre product
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the exactness required at ker(gamma) into the objects s and t and the morphisms n, zeta and vartheta that carry the rest of the argument.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of the kernel sequence
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the last step from the exactness of ker(beta) -> ker(gamma) -> coker(alpha) to the exactness of the full six-term sequence of the statement.

core_obligations: Existence and uniqueness of the connecting map (proof lines 1268-1327): uniqueness is read off from the projection being an epimorphism and the coprojection a monomorphism, the maps a and b are produced from the exactness of the third row and from the cartesianness of the upper right quadrangle, and the resulting delta with delta composed with pi equal to pi'' composed with a is shown to commute with the required diagram.
The composite delta g' is zero (proof lines 1329-1335): the cartesian square gives c : ker(beta) -> p with pi' c = h and pi c = g', and the computation with the coprojection shows that delta g' = 0.

Exactness at ker(gamma) (proof lines 1337-1339): for d : r -> ker(gamma) with delta d = 0 the author applies the fibre-product criterion twice, first to the epimorphism p -> ker(gamma) and then to x -> u -> coker(alpha), to build the auxiliary objects s and t and a morphism vartheta into ker(beta) with g' vartheta = d m epsilon, which is the required exactness.
The remaining kernels and cokernels (proof lines 1340-1342): the author concludes from the previous step, the cited kernel-sequence lemma and duality.
proof_roadmap: Produce the connecting map from the exact row and the cartesian square, and get uniqueness from the epimorphism and monomorphism in the diagram.
Show that the composite with the map out of ker(beta) vanishes.
Test exactness at ker(gamma) through the fibre-product criterion and finish with the kernel-sequence lemma and duality.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the snake lemma for a commutative diagram with exact rows in an abelian category, giving both the connecting map with its defining universal property and the exactness of the resulting six-term sequence with the two extra injectivity and surjectivity statements (statement lines 1228-1265). The proof is a complete argument: uniqueness and the construction of the connecting map are read off from the displayed diagram (proof lines 1268-1327), the vanishing of one composite is computed (proof lines 1329-1335), and exactness at the middle term is obtained by two applications of the fibre-product criterion which produce the auxiliary objects and morphism (proof lines 1337-1339), after which the conclusion follows from a named kernel-sequence lemma and duality (proof lines 1340-1342). The non-formal content is the construction of delta through the two cartesian squares and the exactness test. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
